mcq: Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the exercise that an athlete performs in a training session."
A training load is the exercise that an athlete performs in a training session.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the ratio of water, bone, muscle (Lean tissue) and fat in the body."
Body composition is the ratio of water, bone, muscle (Lean tissue) and fat in the body.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a combination of rhythmic exercise and static stretching through a full range which begins to raise the heart rate and raise muscle temperature."
Warm-up is a combination of rhythmic exercise and static stretching through a full range which begins to raise the heart rate and raise muscle temperature.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to the ways in which teachers and coaches learn the teaching knowledge and skills that are needed to support them to learn effectively (Armour, 2013)."
Sports Pedagogy refers to the ways in which teachers and coaches learn the teaching knowledge and skills that are needed to support them to learn effectively (Armour, 2013).
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are those factors restricted to the participants while extrinsic factors require outside agents."
Intrinsic factors are those factors restricted to the participants while extrinsic factors require outside agents.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the ability to perform sports, occupation and daily activities."
Physical fitness is the ability to perform sports, occupation and daily activities.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the amount of time it takes to respond to stimulus."
Reaction time is the amount of time it takes to respond to stimulus.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a systematic process with the objective of improving an individual's fitness in a selected activity."
Training is a systematic process with the objective of improving an individual's fitness in a selected activity.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ means only how fast one can run - True/False/Not sure 4."
Speed means only how fast one can run - True/False/Not sure 4.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the failure to warm up properly as well as engaging in an activity the body is not properly conditioned for."
Improper warm-up is the failure to warm up properly as well as engaging in an activity the body is not properly conditioned for.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to the development of physical fitness through the adaptation of the body and its various systems to an exercise programme (Encyclopaedia Britannica, 2020)."
Physical conditioning refers to the development of physical fitness through the adaptation of the body and its various systems to an exercise programme (Encyclopaedia Britannica, 2020).

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a contest or game in which an individual partakes in certain physical activities according to a specific set of rules and compete against each other."
Sport is a contest or game in which an individual partakes in certain physical activities according to a specific set of rules and compete against each other.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the process of applying training loads on an athlete's fitness level to challenge a response from the body."
Loading is the process of applying training loads on an athlete's fitness level to challenge a response from the body.
fib: ______ is the exercise that increases the body strength, speed, endurance or any other physical attribute.
Conditioning exercise
Conditioning exercise is the exercise that increases the body strength, speed, endurance or any other physical attribute.
______ means putting the body under more stress than normal in order for adaptive changes to be made.
Overload principle simply
Overload principle simply means putting the body under more stress than normal in order for adaptive changes to be made.
______ is the coming of an athlete into hard contact with object or another person which can cause damage to connective tissue or joint causing dislocation.
Impact
Impact is the coming of an athlete into hard contact with object or another person which can cause damage to connective tissue or joint causing dislocation.
______ is the science that studies the effects of internal and external force on human performance.
Biomechanical analysis in physical education
Biomechanical analysis in physical education is the science that studies the effects of internal and external force on human performance.
______ is defined as damage to the tissues of the body that occurs as a result of sport or exercise (Engebretsen, Laprade, Mccrory & Meeuwisse, 2012).
sports injury
A sports injury is defined as damage to the tissues of the body that occurs as a result of sport or exercise (Engebretsen, Laprade, Mccrory & Meeuwisse, 2012).
______ is a way of improving performance and preventing injury.
Training to acquire relevant skill
Training to acquire relevant skill is a way of improving performance and preventing injury.
______ is the process of training to become physically fit by a regimen of exercise.
Conditioning
Conditioning is the process of training to become physically fit by a regimen of exercise.
______ is a person's level of adaptability and capability of living a certain lifestyle.
Fitness
Fitness is a person's level of adaptability and capability of living a certain lifestyle.
______ is the result of repetitive micro trauma to tendons, bones, and joints (Matava, 2019).
Overuse
Overuse is the result of repetitive micro trauma to tendons, bones, and joints (Matava, 2019).
______ is the modification of training to account for an athlete unique capacity for and response to training.
Individualization
Individualization is the modification of training to account for an athlete unique capacity for and response to training.
______ is the act, process or art of imparting knowledge and skill.
Pedagogy
Pedagogy is the act, process or art of imparting knowledge and skill.
______ is the range of motion at the joint.
Flexibility
Flexibility is the range of motion at the joint.
______ is the most common causes of poor technique and performance.
Restricted flexibility
Restricted flexibility is the most common causes of poor technique and performance.
